name: REST Assured API Test Automation
certifications: No official REST Assured certification; assessed by capstone projects
ISTQB Advanced Level Test Automation Engineering (CTAL-TAE)

beginner.summary: For testers and developers starting API automation in Java with REST Assured. Covers Java essentials for API tests, Maven projects, the given-when-then style, requests with parameters, headers and bodies, response checks with Hamcrest, JSON path, POJOs with Jackson, authentication, specifications, logging and filters, JSON Schema validation, chained CRUD flows, data-driven tests with TestNG, file uploads, cookies, XML responses, negative tests, reports and running suites with Maven in CI.
prerequisites: Understands HTTP methods, status codes and JSON
Basic Java or another programming language
Has tested APIs by hand, for example with Postman
outcomes: Write readable REST Assured tests that check status, headers, bodies and schemas
Serialise and deserialise JSON with POJOs and reuse request and response specifications
Build chained and data-driven API test flows with TestNG
Run the suite with Maven in CI and publish Allure reports

days.topic: REST Assured Overview and Maven Project Setup
subtopics: What REST Assured is and where it fits in API testing
REST Assured compared with Postman and other API tools
Installing a JDK and IntelliJ IDEA
Adding REST Assured, TestNG and Hamcrest dependencies
Project folders for tests and resources
Writing and running a first GET test
Running tests from the IDE and with mvn test
The course API and project overview

days.deliverable: Maven project with a first passing test
checks: mvn test compiles and runs the test
The test checks the status code
A deliberately wrong status assertion is explained from its output
objectives: Set up a REST Assured project

days.topic: Java Essentials for API Testers: Classes, Collections and Exceptions

days.deliverable: Helper class, test and fixed examples
checks: The helper class compiles and is used by a test

intermediate.summary: For testers and SDETs who write REST Assured tests and now build a maintainable framework. Covers framework layers, configuration and environments, API client classes, test data builders and Faker, JUnit 5 as an alternative runner, parallel execution, WireMock stubs, Testcontainers, OAuth 2.0 flows, contract checks against OpenAPI, Pact contract testing in Java, Spring MockMvc tests, GraphQL testing, database checks, asynchronous APIs, retries and flakiness, combined API and UI tests with Selenium, Kotlin and Groovy options, and quality checks on test code.
prerequisites: Writes REST Assured tests with specifications and POJOs
Comfortable with Java, Maven and Git
Has run an API suite in CI
outcomes: Design a layered REST Assured framework that a team can extend
Isolate tests from unstable dependencies with WireMock and Testcontainers
Add contract tests with OpenAPI validation and Pact
Run large suites in parallel with reliable data and clear reports

objectives: Make the framework easy to extend

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Layered API Framework with Stubs and Contracts

advanced.summary: For automation leads and SDETs who own API quality across many Java services. Covers framework architecture for many services, shared libraries, test impact analysis, contract testing at scale, API performance with Gatling or JMeter DSL, security testing, chaos and resilience checks, event-driven systems with Kafka, test environments and data at scale, observability for tests, AI-assisted test generation, governance, migration from other tools, extending REST Assured, regulated APIs, metrics, team enablement, strategy and troubleshooting.
prerequisites: Has built and maintained a REST Assured framework used by a team
Strong Java, Maven and CI skills
outcomes: Architect API test automation across many services and teams
Add performance, security, resilience and event-driven testing to API quality
Govern API tests and keep large suites fast and trusted
Lead API automation strategy and capability
